blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Charyapada is the earliest known collection of Bengali mystic poems, discovered by Mahamahopadhyaya Haraprasad Shastri in Nepal in 1907.
Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote 'Anandamath' in 1882, which featured the song 'Vande Mataram' that inspired the Indian independence movement.
Rabindranath Tagore became the first non-European and Asian to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for 'Gitanjali'.
Kazi Nazrul Islam, known as 'Bidrohi Kabi' (The Rebel Poet), authored groundbreaking poems such as 'Bidrohi' and 'Pralayollas'.
Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay earned the epithet 'Aporajeya Kotha Shilpi' for his social novels like 'Devdas', 'Pather Dabi', and 'Charitraheen'.
Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's 'Durgeshnondini' (1865) is considered the first major Bengali novel.
The song 'Vande Mataram' from 'Anandamath' was first sung politically by Rabindranath Tagore at the 1896 session of the Indian National Congress.
Haraprasad Shastri discovered the Charyapada manuscript in 1907 at the Royal Court Library of Nepal.

cells: [EXAM TIP] Satyajit Ray's "Pather Panchali" (1955) was based on Bibhutibhushan Bandyopadhyay's novel and won 11 international awards. Satyajit Ray received an Honorary Oscar in 1992. Both asked in WB exams.
